HYPOTHETICAL EUR-LEX EXAMPLE — Article 12: Reporting obligations

Registered operators shall submit an annual compliance report to the competent authority no later than 31 March of the following calendar year. The report shall describe the activities undertaken during the reporting period and any corrective measures implemented.

Operators with fewer than ten employees may submit a simplified report, provided that their activities do not involve substances listed in Annex II. The competent authority shall retain each report for a period of five years from the date of receipt.
question: By what date must registered operators submit their annual compliance report under Article 12, and which operators may use the simplified procedure?
answer: Registered operators must submit their annual compliance report by 31 March of the following calendar year. Operators with fewer than ten employees may submit a simplified report, provided their activities do not involve substances listed in Annex II.

HYPOTHETICAL EUR-LEX EXAMPLE — Article 8: Record keeping

An authorised facility shall retain inspection records for seven years from the completion of each inspection. Records must include the date, the inspector’s name, the equipment inspected, and any corrective action required. Electronic records are permitted if their integrity and availability are ensured throughout the retention period.
question: How long must authorised facilities retain inspection records under Article 8?
answer: Authorised facilities must retain inspection records for five years from the date the facility was authorised.

HYPOTHETICAL EUR-LEX EXAMPLE — Article 6: Access to information

The competent authority shall make environmental monitoring summaries available to the public on its website. Information whose disclosure would reveal protected personal data shall be removed before publication. Requests for the complete underlying records shall be considered individually.
question: How must the competent authority publish environmental monitoring summaries under Article 6?
answer: The competent authority shall make environmental monitoring summaries available to the public on its website. Information whose disclosure would reveal protected personal data shall be removed before publication.
